text:
Samira: heads up — customer acme-inc reporting a burst of 504s/5xx from hosted inference cluster r-hosted-2 since ~10:58 UTC. Ticket INC-5231. They say requests are timing out and retries are ballooning. Anyone oncall?
Maria: oncall here, pulling logs now. Which endpoint and model?
Samira: /v1/generate, model=open-medium-v2, streaming off. Example request id req_abc123. Tail latency >15s then gateway times out.
Ben: I'm seeing a bunch of scale-up events in the metrics. HPA + KEDA triggered but pods are not becoming Ready quickly — model load looks like the culprit. KEDA activationThreshold=5 and cooldown=30s, but pod warmup is ~40-50s so we keep getting repeated scaleups that don't finish in time.
Luis: logs/snippet from one of the failing pods:
```
2026-03-15T10:59:12Z INFO starting model load: open-medium-v2
2026-03-15T11:00:00Z ERROR readiness probe failed: GET /healthz -> 500
2026-03-15T11:00:02Z INFO model loaded in 42.3s, warming KV cache
2026-03-15T11:00:05Z WARN connection queue overflow: write tcp 10.0.2.14:443->10.0.8.9:50432: connection reset by peer
```
kubectl: HPA desired=10 current=2, ScaledObject shows triggers firing repeatedly.
Maria: we rolled quant-runtime v1.3 to r-hosted-2 at 09:40 — could that have increased cold-start?
Ben: yes, that build increased cold-start by ~30% in perf tests (we flagged it). But autoscaler config for that pool wasn't adjusted.
Samira: customer is escalated — billing showing lots of retries, they may throttle traffic. Need a quick mitigation plan.
Luis: short term options: bump HPA minReplicas to 4 for that deployment; reduce KEDA activationThreshold to 2 and pollInterval to 2s temporarily; or add a pre-warm job that hits /warmup endpoint to prime model cache. Also tweak startupProbe/readinessProbe so model load doesn't spam 5xx while still blocking traffic until ready.
Ben: I'm going to patch HPA minReplicas and adjust KEDA settings. Also we can temporarily pin the customer to a smaller model variant to reduce startup time.
Maria: I'll open a small runtime patch: startupProbe periodSeconds=5, timeoutSeconds=10, failureThreshold=10 for the hosted pool. Also add annotation workload.kubernetes.io/prewarm=true so infra can opt-in to keep some pods hot.
Samira: Customer message ready: apology + mitigation. Suggest we give them a short TTL token to test. Send? :pray:
Customer-ops: here's a reproducer curl they ran: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"model":"open-medium-v2","prompt":"hello","max_tokens":512}' -v
```
Luis: reproduced locally — when scaling 1->6 we see same 504s. Backend logs show model load blocks main thread, connection backlog grows, upstream gateway returns 504. Snippet: 
```
upstream request timed out after 15s, conn_queue_len=102, accept failures=12
```
Ben: patch applied at 11:30 UTC: HPA minReplicas increased to 4 (kubectl apply output ok), KEDA pollInterval set to 2s for ScaledObject r-hosted-2 (temporary). Watching metrics.
Maria: metrics: 5xx rate dropping, p95 latency down to ~2.1s. Customer confirmed partial recovery. :white_check_mark:
Samira: good. Next steps: decide long-term fix — either revert the quant-runtime rollout or add a pre-warm service + adjust autoscaler policies by model type. I'll open a follow-up postmortem and link to INC-5231.
Ben: creating incident doc and config diffs. I'll own the rollback if needed; @Luis you'll own postmortem writeup.
Luis: ack. I'll include kube diffs, logs, and repro steps.
ticket-bot: INCIDENT-2026 created: autoscale-warmup-mismatch. Owners: Ben, Luis. Severity: P2.
Samira: thanks everyone. Leaving the temporary patches in place until we have the postmortem and a stable mitigation. Will update customer thread once postmortem action items are defined.
Maria: note for follow-ups — add a unit to Redwood Optimize to recommend per-model warmup config and autoscaler profiles.
Ben: linking PRs and will schedule a rollback window if quant-runtime is the root cause.
Samira: closing internal thread once customer confirms full recovery. Thanks all. :bow:
